versions.name: RXV2-0.9.154-wifi-1s
versions.notes: Tunes the auto-WiFi from 0.9.153 and documents it. The boot listen-for-transmitter window is now 1 second (was 5): WiFi comes up almost instantly when there's no transmitter, which means the transmitter must be switched ON before the receiver to run radio-only — and switching the transmitter on first is normal RC practice anyway. Adds a clear 'WiFi and your transmitter' section to the WiFi page Help so users understand why WiFi may be off (a transmitter was on at switch-on) and how it returns by itself ~10s after the link is lost.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.153-wifi-auto
versions.notes: WiFi is now managed automatically around the transmitter. (1) At power-up the receiver listens for the transmitter for 5 seconds; if it hears one, it switches WiFi OFF for the session and runs radio-only — the cleanest band and full 501 Hz. (2) If, in that radio-only mode, the transmitter link is then lost for 10 seconds (you've landed, or switched the TX off), WiFi comes back on by itself so you can reach the receiver from your phone — no power-cycle needed. Simulator sessions keep WiFi on throughout (so you can still use the web UI while driving the sim). Note: a real in-air dropout lasting 10 s would also re-enable WiFi mid-flight; the threshold is easy to raise if you'd prefer a longer wait.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.152-ap-only-ux
versions.notes: Polishes the new 'AP mode only' option. (1) Plain-English explanation on the WiFi page — spells out that AP mode means the receiver makes its own little WiFi network your phone joins directly (no home router), why you'd tick it at the field, and that you'll need to switch your phone's WiFi after saving. (2) The save page no longer sits there waiting: when you turn AP-only on it stops polling the old address (which has gone) and instead clearly tells you to open your phone's WiFi settings, join the receiver's network (named), and go to 192.168.4.1. (3) Bug fix: the status page now shows the receiver's REAL access-point name (its model name, e.g. your renamed receiver) instead of always showing the old default 'LDRC_RX'.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.150-ap-only
versions.notes: Adds an 'AP mode only' tick-box to the WiFi page. When on, the receiver skips trying to join your home WiFi and comes straight up as its own access point — handy at the flying field, where the home network is miles away and the receiver would otherwise spend every boot fruitlessly retrying it. Your saved home SSID/password are kept; just untick it to use home WiFi again. The choice is saved in NVS and survives reboots/updates.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.149-wifi-advice
versions.notes: Adds a setup tip on the WiFi page (and its help): WiFi is steadiest with the transmitter switched off, because the control radio and WiFi share the 2.4GHz band and a live transmitter link can make WiFi drop in and out. Advises using the transmitter or the phone when you can — both together works fine, but expect WiFi to be less consistent. Text only; no behaviour change. (Includes the data/web files, so the page updates.)

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.148-flash-fixed
versions.notes: FIXES the channels flashing to zero on the Configurator. Root cause, pinned down by on-board logging: whenever WiFi tried to reconnect — and WiFi drops a lot while flying because the radio desenses it — the reconnect ran inline and FROZE the main loop for ~208ms each attempt, long enough to pause RC output and starve the radio, so the flight-controller saw a brief RX-loss and the channels flashed to zero, then recovered. WiFi reconnection is now fully non-blocking: the loop never stalls and RC output stays continuous no matter how much WiFi flaps. Verified over 20+ minutes connected with WiFi flapping throughout — zero output stalls, zero spurious drops. (Also rolls up the supporting robustness work from 0.9.136-0.9.140: failsafe keyed off the real packet stream, a short board-ID burst then continuous telemetry like V1, gentler dual-radio failover, out-of-range frames rejected so the last good values are held, and no FC version-polling while a link is live.)

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.140-no-fc-probe-flying
versions.notes: Found the real cause of the channels flashing to zero in the Rotorflight Configurator. The actual RC output was never glitching (steady 250Hz, link solid) — it was only the Configurator's *display*. The receiver was polling the flight-controller over MSP every few seconds to read its firmware version; that made the receiver a second MSP 'master' on the FC, colliding with the Configurator's own MSP polling of the same FC, so the Configurator periodically read an empty frame and showed all channels at zero. The receiver now never probes the FC while a transmitter link is live (it already behaved this way on shipping firmware; a dev-only setting was bypassing it). FC-version detection still happens when not flying, which is when the web page needs it. Note: the model itself was always controlled correctly throughout — this was a bench-display artifact, not a flight risk.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.139-hold-last-good
versions.notes: Channels flashing to zero, fixed the way V1 does it: hold the last good value. Two V1 behaviours the receiver was missing are now restored. (1) Crazy-value rejection: the transmitter periodically sends non-channel frames (bind/ID/parameter data); if one was misread as channel data it drove every channel to zero for an instant. Like V1's CheckForCrazyValues, any decoded frame with a channel outside the legal 500-2500us range is now rejected and the last good values are held. (2) The output no longer goes briefly silent on a momentary gap: the failsafe timeout is raised from 500ms to V1's 1500ms, and below it the receiver keeps streaming the held channel values (exactly as V1 keeps sending its SBUS frames) instead of detaching the CRSF line. True signal loss (>1.5s) still drops the link so the flight-controller can fail-safe.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.138-swap-storm-fix
versions.notes: The actual cause of the channels flashing to zero. When the active radio missed packets for a moment the receiver would try the other transceiver — correct — but it kept re-trying every 50ms in a tight storm (~20 swaps/second), and each swap briefly stops listening and reconfigures, which tore down the CRSF output stream long enough for the flight-controller to register a momentary RX-loss (the flash). It also flooded the event log so nothing else could be seen. Now: it tries each transceiver once per glitch, then — if no packet comes back (transmitter gone/out of range) — backs off to a slow once-a-second probe instead of storming, and re-arms instant failover the moment a real packet returns. Dead-link swaps no longer spam the log. Fast genuine failover between two good transceivers is unchanged.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.137-mac-burst-telemetry
versions.notes: The real fix for channels flashing to zero every ~10-15s with the sticks still (0.9.136 only moved the symptom). Root cause: the receiver was broadcasting its board ID to the transmitter continuously whenever you weren't actively moving a stick, and never sending telemetry — so the transmitter, starved of telemetry, hiccuped the link about every 10-15s (a brief RX-loss that flashed every channel to zero) and also never showed the RX version or the per-transceiver active-time counters until you wiggled a stick. Now the board ID is sent only as a short dense burst at the start of each connection (and re-sent on every reconnect), exactly like V1, then telemetry flows continuously. Result: rock-steady channels when not moving, and the version + counters appear immediately without touching the sticks. Note: the transmitter's 'Model IDs' identify screen now re-reads the ID on reconnect rather than continuously.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.136-failsafe-flash-fix
versions.notes: Fixes all channels briefly flashing to zero in the flight-controller (e.g. Rotorflight Configurator) every few seconds while the sticks are held still — a momentary false RXLOSS. The receiver was deciding 'link lost' from the last packet that carried channel data, but with the sticks still the transmitter sends only changed channels, so the gaps between changes (filled with parameter/no-change packets) made the link look dropped for an instant. Failsafe is now judged from the actual packet stream from the bound transmitter (which never stops while connected), so the channels stay rock-steady when you're not moving the sticks. Important for steady hovers.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.135-radio-timer-fix
versions.notes: Fixes the per-transceiver 'active time' counters on the TX screen sitting frozen at 0 on a solid link. The active radio's dwell time is now accrued continuously every loop (not via a live-delta that didn't land on a no-swap link), so one counter always ticks once per second while connected — matching V1.
